subject: general
question: Indian Conservation Conference–2025, highlighting traditional knowledge and scientific approaches, took place in which month of 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Conservation Conference–2025** was organized in **June 2025** as a premier event to foster dialogue between **environmental scientists** and **indigenous communities**.
 
• The core theme of the conference revolved around the integration of **traditional ecological knowledge (TEK)** with **modern scientific methodologies** to tackle the rising threats of **climate change** and **habitat fragmentation**.
 
• It emphasized that **indigenous practices**, honed over centuries by **tribal populations** in **India**, provide invaluable insights into **sustainable harvesting** and **biodiversity preservation**.
 
• The **scientific approaches** discussed included the use of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** for **wildlife tracking**, **satellite imagery** for monitoring **forest cover**, and **biotechnology** for **ex-situ conservation**.
 
• The conference concluded with the drafting of a **Roadmap for 2030**, aligning India's domestic conservation goals with the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Environment Day:** Observed annually on **June 5**, this international day served as a backdrop for the **2025 conference**, highlighting India’s **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** initiative launched in **2022**.
 
• **Legal Framework in India:** Conservation efforts in the country are primarily governed by the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972** and the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**, both of which provide a legal basis for protecting **endangered species** and **ecosystems**.
 
• **Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL):** India has pioneered the protection of **traditional knowledge** through the **TKDL**, preventing the **bio-piracy** of ancient medicinal and ecological practices.
 
• **Role of MoEFCC:** The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the nodal agency responsible for planning, promoting, and coordinating India's **environmental** and **forestry programs**.
 
• **International Collaboration:** India actively participates in **COP (Conference of Parties)** meetings under the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**, striving for **Net Zero** emissions by the **year 2070**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots:** India hosts **four** of the world’s **36 biodiversity hotspots**: the **Himalayas**, the **Western Ghats**, the **Indo-Burma region**, and the **Sundaland** (including the Nicobar Islands).
 
• **Community Reserves:** The **2025 conference** highlighted the success of **Community Reserves**, where local residents take the lead in **conservation**, demonstrating the power of **decentralized environmental management**.
 
• **Article 48A:** The **Constitution of India**, under **Directive Principles of State Policy**, mandates that the **State** shall endeavor to protect and improve the **environment** and safeguard **forests** and **wildlife**.
 
• **Article 51A(g):** It is a **Fundamental Duty** of every citizen of **India** to protect and improve the **natural environment**, including **forests**, **lakes**, **rivers**, and **wildlife**.
 
• **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA):** Established in **2003** and headquartered in **Chennai**, the **NBA** performs a facilitative and advisory role for the **Government of India** on issues of **conservation** and **sustainable use** of biological resources.
